clue.text: Old person looking very unkempt, as entitled

parts.note: someone who looks a fright is a dishevelled sight, so such a person is called a fright

explanation.surface: A scruffy elderly person is described, as though by some right of title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of right' is a legal phrase meaning by entitlement, as in a member of a body of right.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held of right is held by legitimate claim, which is what being entitled to it means.

clue.text: Mythical court turned up by chance

parts.note: to turn up is to arrive, so turned up means came
lot means chance or fate, as in casting lots

explanation.surface: A legendary royal court is stumbled upon purely by accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' looks like a reversal signal, but it is the synonym for arrived; 'by' simply links the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend places King Arthur's court and castle at the fabled site of that name.

clue.text: Note I must be detained by famous shopkeeper

indicators.note: being detained by something means being held inside it, so the note and the number go within the other word

parts.note: a star is a famous person, used here loosely for famous
TI is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
the Roman numeral I stands for one

explanation.surface: A celebrated retailer is told a note must be held up by him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Famous' seems to describe the shopkeeper but is the container STAR; I stands for ONE via the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A seller of paper, pens and office supplies keeps a particular kind of shop.

clue.text: Email blitz overwhelms son in sudden attack

indicators.note: to overwhelm something is to engulf it, so the son's letter goes inside the junk mail

parts.note: spam is a flood of unwanted email
S is the abbreviation for son in genealogies

explanation.surface: A deluge of junk email swamps a young man, bringing on a fit.
explanation.definitionFit: A spasm is a sudden fit or seizure, an attack of coughing, pain or emotion.

clue.text: Quietly witty notice shows spirit

parts.note: dry humour is understated wit
an ad is a notice in a newspaper

explanation.surface: A deadpan advertisement reveals something about one's character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' looks like mood or character but is a supernatural being.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a dryad is a tree nymph, a nature spirit living in woodland.

clue.text: Gambler, cheated at first, would do well to

indicators.note: placed at first means the word for cheated is put in front of the gambler

parts.note: to be had is to be swindled, so had means cheated
a better is one who bets

explanation.surface: Advice to a punter who was swindled at the start of the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom expressing advice or obligation, 'you'd better go', means it would be wise to.

clue.text: Grit in carriages caused damage? An arrogant assumption

indicators.note: the grit is placed in among the rearranged letters
damaged carriages are wrecked, so their letters are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: sand is grit

explanation.surface: Wondering whether grit got into railway carriages and wrecked them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caused damage?' marks the anagram; the rearranged carriages split in two, with the grit lodged between the parts. The question mark admits the surface's wreck is only a fancy.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting on affected, superior manners is assuming a status one lacks, a haughty pretension.

clue.text: In train, man played trumpet aloud and moved, to this?

indicators.note: the pieces go in the train, held between its first and last letters

parts.note: the Tube is the London Underground railway
he is a pronoun for a man

indicators.note: said aloud, the word for played the trumpet gives a colour's spelling

parts.note: one blew a trumpet to play it

indicators.note: moved means the letters of and are shifted about

explanation.surface: On a train, a man played the trumpet and was moved to dance, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' rearranges AND to DAN. The whole clue pictures dancing, and the waltz is what one might be moved to.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Strauss's famous waltz is the classic piece people are moved to dance to.

clue.text: Essential component of maximum break for international players

definitions.meaning: a snooker maximum of 147 needs a black potted after every red, so every black is required
New Zealand's national rugby union team is known by this name

explanation.surface: A snooker term that also names a famous rugby side.
explanation.walkthrough: In snooker a maximum break pots all fifteen reds, each followed by the black worth seven points.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Zealand rugby team wear black kit and are called by that nickname internationally.

clue.text: Charlie's predecessor once who has a bun in the oven?

definitions.meaning: in the old Able-...-Charlie phonetic alphabet, B came just before C

definitions.text: who has a bun in the oven?
definitions.meaning: taken literally, the person with buns baking is a professional bread maker

explanation.surface: Asking who came before Charlie, and who is expecting a baby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bun in the oven' is slang for being pregnant; read literally it points to a bread maker.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who bakes bread and buns literally has them in the oven; the old radio alphabet word for B preceded Charlie.

clue.text: Hard to get a horse to turn round in the country

indicators.note: the hard letter gets into the turned-round pair
turning round reverses the a and horse, so they read backwards

parts.note: a nag is a horse, usually an old one
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: It's difficult to make a horse turn round in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn round' reverses A NAG to GANA; H goes inside after the G.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghana is a West African nation, formerly the Gold Coast.

clue.text: Told story of small, weak fleet covering separate areas

indicators.note: the weak fleet pair covers an area placed between its two words
separate says the areas are split up, one of them going inside the word for weak

parts.note: puny means weak
A is the abbreviation for area
RN is the Royal Navy, a fleet
the second A, also standing for area

explanation.surface: A tale about a little feeble navy spread over several regions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'separate' tells you the two areas do not sit together: one goes inside the weak word, the other between the weak word and the fleet, which together cover it.
explanation.definitionFit: To spin a yarn is to tell a tale, often a tall one, so the phrase means narrated a story.

clue.text: Unsteady rocking not new — it's a regular occurrence

indicators.note: rocking shakes the word unsteady so its letters move about

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new; 'not' says it is the letter left over

explanation.surface: An unsteady rocking motion, nothing novel, happens routinely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocking' rearranges UNSTEADY, and 'not new' says one N is left out of the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A day of the week comes round every seven days, so it recurs on a regular basis.

clue.text: Gloom as some captives send a signal back

indicators.note: back means the stretch is read from right to left
some of the words means a stretch of their letters is used

explanation.surface: Prisoners sending a signal is a gloomy business.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading CAPTIVES SEND A SIGNAL backwards from the last S gives the run.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadness is a synonym for gloom, a low, melancholy state of mind.

clue.text: Willing to play ball — and allowed to

definitions.meaning: to have someone ... is to have their agreement and cooperation
in football a player in the legal position may play the ball

explanation.surface: Someone willing to cooperate, and permitted to do so.
explanation.walkthrough: In football and rugby, being onside means a player is legally placed to play the ball, which the second definition, 'allowed to', completes.
explanation.definitionFit: Being onside means supportive or cooperative, and in sport being legally positioned to play.

clue.text: Cash earned is extremely convenient

parts.note: ready, or the readies, is slang for cash
made means earned, as in made a fortune

explanation.surface: Money earned through work is highly handy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The ready' is British slang for cash in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bought already prepared needs no work, so it is highly convenient.

clue.text: Coin from learner accepted by girls' leader

indicators.note: being accepted means being taken in, so the learner goes inside the leader

parts.note: a Guider is an adult leader in the Girl Guides
L is the learner sign on British cars

explanation.surface: A coin from a learner is taken by the head of the girls' group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'girls' leader' looks like a first-letter instruction (G) but is GUIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: The guilder was the Dutch currency unit before the euro.

clue.text: Very poor holidaymaker finally admitted to dislike of camping?

indicators.note: being admitted is being let inside, so the last letter goes into the phrase

parts.note: a hatred of camping would be a tent hate

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word holidaymaker

explanation.surface: A poor holidaymaker who hates camping at the end of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: The R goes into HATE, after TENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenth-rate means of the lowest quality, far below first-rate, hence very poor.

clue.text: Fellow left-winger dispensed with the centre

parts.note: co- is a prefix meaning joint or fellow, as in co-worker
a red is a socialist or communist

explanation.surface: A comrade on the political left who has given up moderation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' suggests middle letters or politics, but it is the core of an apple.
explanation.definitionFit: An apple that has been cored has had its central part removed.

clue.text: Erasmus, mistaken, finds a rubber

indicators.note: mistaken means wrong, so the name's letters are set wrongly

explanation.surface: The scholar Erasmus, in error, discovers an eraser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a rubber' looks like an eraser, which fits the scholar, but it is one who massages.
explanation.definitionFit: A masseur rubs and kneads muscles for a living.

clue.text: Pressure in watercourse jumped

indicators.note: in places the pressure letter inside the watercourse

parts.note: a leat is an open channel bringing water to a mill
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Under pressure in a stream, someone jumped.
explanation.definitionFit: Leapt is a past tense of leap, meaning jumped.

clue.text: Job around first day of spring perhaps to find tree

indicators.note: the job goes around the date, enclosing it

parts.note: a task is a job
MAR I is March the first, taken as the start of spring

explanation.surface: A job on the first day of spring might be finding a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: MAR I reads as 1 March, meteorological spring's opening day; 'perhaps' admits it is one definition among several.
explanation.definitionFit: The tamarisk is a feathery-leaved shrub or small tree of coasts and deserts.

clue.text: Book promotions saving daughter a tiny amount

indicators.note: to save is to keep inside, so the promotions hold the other pieces

parts.note: deals are special offers in shops
a sou was a small French coin, hence a trifling sum

explanation.surface: Offers that save a daughter a small amount of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Gogol's novel about a scheme to buy dead serfs carries that title.

clue.text: Goodness — carpet in church that may be delivered by bishop

definitions.text: that may be delivered by bishop

indicators.note: the exclamation and the carpet go inside the church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
heck is a mild exclamation like goodness
a mat is a small carpet

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims about a carpet in church that a bishop might deliver.
explanation.walkthrough: The bishop is the chess piece, not the cleric, and it can deliver the final winning move.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess the bishop can give the winning attack on the king that ends the game.

clue.text: Honest view about what's on gallery wall being upside-down

indicators.note: about means the view goes round the other piece

parts.note: a sight is a view

indicators.note: upside-down in a down clue means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: art is what hangs on gallery walls

explanation.surface: An honest opinion about a picture hanging upside-down in a gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being upside-down' turns ART into TRA.
explanation.definitionFit: A straight person is honest and direct, as in being straight with someone.

clue.text: Expression of amusement over fat reformer

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the first piece above the second

parts.note: LOL is the texting abbreviation for laughing out loud
lard is pig fat

explanation.surface: Laughing at an overweight reformer.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lollards were followers of John Wycliffe, pre-Reformation religious reformers in England.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lollard was one of Wycliffe's followers, early campaigners for church reform.

clue.text: Criticise pub freely over visit from police?

indicators.note: in a down clue over puts the first piece above the second
freely means the letters of pub are rearranged without constraint

parts.note: a raid is a police swoop

explanation.surface: Criticising a pub for being too lax about a police visit.
explanation.definitionFit: To upbraid someone is to scold or reproach them, to criticise severely.

clue.text: This shrub crying out to be trimmed?

definitions.text: This shrub crying out to be trimmed?

parts.words: This shrub crying out to be trimmed?
parts.note: the shrub's name, said in two parts, is a plea for pruning

explanation.surface: An overgrown bush begging to be cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: The genus name sounds like a hedge's own request to be cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Prunus is the plant genus that includes plums, cherries and ornamental shrubs.

clue.text: Contract left to progress gradually

parts.note: to ease is to move slowly and carefully, as in easing forward

explanation.surface: A contract left behind to advance step by step.
explanation.definitionFit: A lease is a contract by which property is rented for a set period.

clue.text: Such New Years are undemanding

indicators.note: new means the letters of such are made fresh in a new order

explanation.surface: Such New Year celebrations are easy-going affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Years' reads as the holiday, but 'New' rearranges SUCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A cushy job is easy and comfortable, requiring little effort.
